item.text: === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-EMPHASIS.md === # FEATURE: Emphasis | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parse CommonMark emphasis and strong emphasis in inline content. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CLI.md, FEATURE-THEMATIC-BREAKS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-SETEXT-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-INDENTED-CODE.md, FEATURE-FENCED-CODE.md, FEATURE-HTML-BLOCKS.md, FEATURE-LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITIONS.md, FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md, FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-LISTS.md, FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md, FEATURE-CHARACTER-REFERENCES.md, FEATURE-CODE-SPANS.md | | Provides | CommonMark emphasis and strong emphasis | | Consumes | CommonMark inline content | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Interpret `*` and `_` delimiter runs as emphasis or strong emphasis according to the CommonMark delimiter-run rules. Support nested spans, Unicode whitespace and punctuation, intraword `*` emphasis, the restrictions on intraword `_` emphasis, and the specified precedence and ambiguity rules. ## Parsing and rendering - Determine left- and right-flanking runs from neighboring Unicode whitespace and punctuation. - Apply the opener and closer rules for `*`, `_`, `**`, and `__`, including the rule of three. - Use the smallest valid delimiter spans and minimize nesting where the rules require it. Preserve unmatched delimiter characters as text. - Render emphasis with `` and strong emphasis with ``. Parse their contents as inline content, including other emphasis constructs. - Code spans, links, images, and HTML tags bind more tightly than emphasis. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC emphasis-suite === Intent: All supplied examples in the “Emphasis and strong emphasis” section pass. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: lines import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Emphasis and strong emphasis"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC emphasis-suite === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Use the supplied CommonMark 0.31.2 rules and examples as authoritative. - Preserve escaped delimiter characters and unmatched runs as literal text. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation. - Do not modify supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-LINKS.md === # FEATURE: Links | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parse inline and reference-style CommonMark links. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CLI.md, FEATURE-THEMATIC-BREAKS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-SETEXT-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-INDENTED-CODE.md, FEATURE-FENCED-CODE.md, FEATURE-HTML-BLOCKS.md, FEATURE-LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITIONS.md, FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md, FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-LISTS.md, FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md, FEATURE-CHARACTER-REFERENCES.md, FEATURE-CODE-SPANS.md, FEATURE-EMPHASIS.md | | Provides | Inline and reference links | | Consumes | Document link reference definitions | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse inline links and full, collapsed, and shortcut reference links. Resolve reference labels against the document-wide definitions collected during block parsing. ## Link behavior - Parse inline destinations in angle-bracket or balanced-parenthesis form, optional titles, escapes, and character references as specified. - Match reference labels after Unicode case folding, trimming, and collapsing whitespace. The first matching definition wins. - Support links with empty text or destinations when allowed by the syntax. - Bracketed link text may contain balanced brackets and inline elements. Links cannot contain nested links; code spans, autolinks, and raw HTML tags bind more tightly than link brackets. - Render destinations as `href` and optional titles as `title`, escaping attribute values for HTML. Render link text as inline HTML. - Images use the same syntax but are specified and implemented by the image capability. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC links-suite === Intent: All supplied examples in the “Links” section pass. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: lines import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Links"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC links-suite === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not create links when the syntax is invalid or the reference label is undefined. - Do not allow links to contain nested links. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation or modify supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-IMAGES.md === # FEATURE: Images | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parse inline and reference-style CommonMark images. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CLI.md, FEATURE-THEMATIC-BREAKS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-SETEXT-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-INDENTED-CODE.md, FEATURE-FENCED-CODE.md, FEATURE-HTML-BLOCKS.md, FEATURE-LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITIONS.md, FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md, FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-LISTS.md, FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md, FEATURE-CHARACTER-REFERENCES.md, FEATURE-CODE-SPANS.md, FEATURE-EMPHASIS.md, FEATURE-LINKS.md | | Provides | Inline and reference images | | Consumes | Document link reference definitions | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse inline and reference-style images using the CommonMark link and label rules, including full, collapsed, and shortcut references. ## Image behavior - Support empty descriptions and descriptions containing inline elements, links, and nested image syntax where valid. - Render images as `` elements with `src`, plain-text `alt`, and an optional `title`. The alt text is the description's plain textual content without inline formatting or markup. - Resolve reference labels using the document-wide definitions and matching rules. - Escape `src`, `alt`, and `title` attribute values for HTML. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC images-suite === Intent: All supplied examples in the “Images” section pass. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: lines import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Images"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC images-suite === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the distinction between links and images; image descriptions render as plain-text alt attributes. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation or modify supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-AUTOLINKS.md === # FEATURE: Autolinks | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Convert valid URI and email autolinks into HTML links. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CLI.md, FEATURE-THEMATIC-BREAKS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-SETEXT-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-INDENTED-CODE.md, FEATURE-FENCED-CODE.md, FEATURE-HTML-BLOCKS.md, FEATURE-LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITIONS.md, FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md, FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-LISTS.md, FEATURE-BACKSLASH-ESCAPES.md, FEATURE-CHARACTER-REFERENCES.md, FEATURE-CODE-SPANS.md, FEATURE-EMPHASIS.md, FEATURE-LINKS.md, FEATURE-IMAGES.md | | Provides | URI and email autolinks | | Consumes | CommonMark inline content | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Recognize valid absolute URI and email address autolinks enclosed in angle brackets. Render them as links whose visible text is the URI or address; email links use the `mailto:` scheme. ## Autolink rules - URI schemes begin with an ASCII letter, contain 2–32 characters, and use only ASCII letters, digits, `+`, `.`, or `-`. - URI contents exclude ASCII control characters, spaces, `<`, and `>`. - Email autolinks follow the email address grammar in the CommonMark specification. - Backslash escapes are not interpreted inside autolinks. - Invalid autolinks remain ordinary text and are escaped as HTML text. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC autolinks-suite === Intent: All supplied examples in the “Autolinks” section pass. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: lines import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Autolinks"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC autolinks-suite === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Do not turn plain URI or email text without angle brackets into links. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation or modify supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-RAW-HTML.md === # FEATURE: Raw HTML | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Preserve valid inline HTML tags and raw HTML constructs in Markdown output. | | Depends On | FEATURE-CLI.md, FEATURE-THEMATIC-BREAKS.md, FEATURE-ATX-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-SETEXT-HEADINGS.md, FEATURE-INDENTED-CODE.md, FEATURE-FENCED-CODE.md, FEATURE-HTML-BLOCKS.md, FEATURE-LINK-REFERENCE-DEFINITIONS.md, FEATURE-PARAGRAPHS.md, FEATURE-BLANK-LINES.md, FEATURE-BLOCK-QUOTES.md, FEATURE-LIST-ITEMS.md, FEATURE-LISTS.md | | Provides | Raw inline HTML | | Consumes | CommonMark inline content | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Recognize valid CommonMark inline HTML tags and constructs, including open and closing tags, comments, processing instructions, declarations, and CDATA sections. Preserve recognized markup literally in HTML output. ## Inline HTML behavior - Apply the grammar for tag names, attributes, attribute values, comments, processing instructions, declarations, and CDATA sections. - Raw HTML binds more tightly than emphasis and link bracket parsing. - Text that does not form a valid raw HTML construct is escaped as ordinary text. - Block HTML handling remains owned by the HTML blocks capability. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC raw-html-suite === Intent: All supplied examples in the “Raw HTML” section pass. Suite: scoped Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: lines import subprocess import sys result = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", "./commonmark", "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", "Raw HTML"], capture_output=True, text=True, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC raw-html-suite === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve recognized raw HTML verbatim and escape invalid tag-like text. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation or modify supplied scoring assets. === END ARTIFACT==="
